headline: Raises the debt limits that decide which small businesses and individuals can use two simpler forms of bankruptcy.
what_it_does: This law brings back higher debt limits that expired in 2024. Small businesses can use Subchapter V, a faster type of bankruptcy reorganization, if they owe up to $7.5 million, up from about $3.4 million. People using Chapter 13, a plan to repay debts over time from their income, can owe up to $2.75 million total, up from about $2.1 million. Chapter 13 will now use one combined limit for secured debt, like a mortgage or car loan, and unsecured debt, like credit cards, instead of separate limits.

who_it_affects.group: Small business owners with large debts
who_it_affects.how: Businesses owing between about $3.4 million and $7.5 million can now qualify for Subchapter V small business bankruptcy.

who_it_affects.group: Individuals with regular income who are in serious debt
who_it_affects.how: More people can qualify for a Chapter 13 repayment plan because the total debt limit rises to $2.75 million and secured and unsecured debts are counted together.
More of the people and businesses that owe them money may be able to use these bankruptcy options, which changes how and when debts are repaid.
